speaker: billdobson
text: All right so we're live now. Thank you Jasmine. So welcome everybody to our special meeting. I will now call to order this special meeting of council held under section 26 of the Planning Act on this ninth day of September 2020. Council provided notice of this special meeting in the local newspaper for two consecutive weeks on July the 29th 2020 and August the 5th 2020 in accordance with the prescribed notice requirements. The purpose of this official plan review is to update the existing official plan policies to conform to the provincial policy statement the PPS 2020 and the Lantern County Sustainable Communities official plan as well as to consider comments by the public and agencies. The Planning Act requires that the township update its 2010 official plan at least 10 years after it was first adopted and every five years after that. As the township continues to develop and change it is important to review the effectiveness of the official plan to ensure it is still achieving the township's goals and objectives. The public's input is very important. This meeting provides township residents with an opportunity to participate in the shaping of the future direction for Montague Township. All those registered to address council will be invited to present your opinion on what official plan improvements or updates should be considered by council following the presentation of the planning report by our consultant. Please note we are not making any decisions tonight but reviewing a report and providing direction. This is just the beginning and it's going to be a long process with lots of opportunity from the public. I'm now going to ask our consultant to well I guess before I before I do that we have a couple of a couple of motions but then I will ask the consultant to present his planning report. But first I have a couple of motions here. The first one was moved by Karen Jennings and seconded by Jeff Carroll that the special meeting of council agenda dated September the 9th 2020 be approved as circulated. All in favor. And that is carried. Thank you. And so now I'm going to go to our consultant Forbes Simon from JP2G and welcome to you Forbes and we look forward to your report and I will hand this part of the meeting over to you now. So thank you Forbes and welcome to our planner Carol. Hi Carol. So thank you Forbes.

speaker: forbess
text: I'll let you take over now. Thank you very much Mr. Mayor. Council it's a pleasure to be with you this evening even if it is virtual. It is the the way that we're doing business right now. It's not ideal but it is the method that the province of Ontario has recognized as an acceptable way of doing business in this time of the COVID pandemic. And I want to reiterate what the mayor said. This is the beginning of a six-month planning process and the public is going to have multiple opportunities to be engaged and have input as we go through this and this is just more or less notice that the project has has started. I did submit to you Mr. Mayor and council a formal report. It's dated September 29th. It's addressed to the mayor and council and it's from myself Forbes Simon. I'm the senior planner with the consulting firm JP2G Consultants Inc and we've been retained by the township to undertake the official plan review and update. As you indicated in your opening remarks Mr. Mayor the planning act anticipates that municipalities once they have official plans regularly review and update those documents and it's there is a prescribed process under the planning act to have this exercise completed in a fair and open and transparent way. One of the first steps is to hold a special meeting of council that's intended to provide the public with an opportunity to to be involved in this discussion that you're having. My report that I've presented to you this evening I'm not going to read it verbatim. It is a matter of public record. It will be posted on the township's website under the official plan update page that's been created but there are a couple of points in the report that I think are important this evening to review. The first is that the township's official plan is 10 years old. It is an appropriate time as set out in the planning act to review the official plan and to make sure that the policies are still relevant and reflect the best planning principles that can be stated at this time. There are a couple of important components that an official plan update and review must touch upon. The first is is that the province has provincial plans and provincial planning policies that are updated on a regular basis. Most recently the province updated their provincial policy statement on planning in the beginning of this year 2020 and municipalities are required under the planning act to be consistent with provincial policy statements and so with the new document coming out now is an appropriate time to look to make sure that the official plan is in step with the provincial policy statement. The other thing is is that the county of Lanark's sustainable communities official plan was adopted in 2012 two years after your official plan and it's also a requirement that a lower tier official plan conform to the upper tier official plan and so part of this review looks at the county's planning documents ensures that your policies are in step with the county's document. So being in step with the provincial policy statement, being in step with the county's official plan are two key elements of this review. The third component is to make sure that you as elected officials within the community have an opportunity to express your opinions about the official plan and what's working and what isn't working, what parts of it need to be enhanced and if there are any new directions the township feels that you should be going in. And then the fourth component is the public's right to participate and express their opinion as to the state of the official plan and how it could be improved or changed for the future of the municipality. So the project that we've initiated is intended to address all four of those points. The big part of the project is in terms of looking after compliance with provincial policies is reaching out to the government agencies whether it's the Ministry of Natural Resources and Forestry, Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing, Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Parks. They've all been notified of this project and they've been asked to participate. Agencies and organizations such as the school boards surrounding municipalities have all been notified that this project is in the process of starting. We've also reached out to the conservation Rideau Valley Conservation Authority and also Parks Canada and finally we've reached out to two of the identified first nations that have an interest in the township Montague. The agency comments that we've received to date have not been comprehensive. It's just the beginning of a discussion but we have received a number of comments and they are attached to the report as an appendicy and will be added to as additional comments come in over time. One part of the project that I particularly enjoyed was the opportunity to speak to each of the councillors and to Jasmine and to Carl and your chief building official as well Jim and to get your sort of feet in the ground view of the township and how the official plan is working and I was impressed with the comments that were given and the thoughtfulness and the desire by all of council to make Montague Township the best it can be and prepare itself for future growth pressures that continue to evolve and change in eastern Ontario. The public comments we're asking this evening Mr. Mayor that council provide the public an opportunity to have their input up until September 30th. We have to pick a some date to be able to close off this initial review process and we're hopeful that we could have public comments by the end of the month. I've been in discussions with Jasmine about having a follow-up notice in the paper next week that would again highlight the project and request comments from the public by September 30th. That doesn't mean that that's the end of their opportunity to be engaged. There will be many opportunities for them as we proceed going forward to express their opinions. I would like Mr. Mayor now to highlight the 12 preliminary issues that have been identified to date. I think it's important for everybody to understand that these are just issues and how the issues are addressed and the changes made to the official plan have not been determined yet. This is just putting on the board the things that we need to look at. The first one is a very clear expression by pretty well everybody that there needs to be an opportunity to expand and diversify the commercial and industrial base of the township. There's also a desire to make sure that the industrial and commercial areas are visually attractive which stimulates future investment. There's also this idea that we need to look at expanded opportunities for people to work at home whether it's in a hamlet setting or in a rural or agricultural setting and expanding the opportunities for people to live and work at home. It's probably no more important that we do it than this day and age when everybody is pretty well working at home or many of us have been. There is also an expression that the township has a lot of scattered residential development and there is a desire to promote more urban areas, expand that or have the hamlets grow. To do so it was indicated that communal services are important to being able to have a higher density of development more in keeping with what you see in urban areas. You need to have something other than private services to be able to help you achieve those goals. The idea of Rosedale being a prime location for increased development activity came up. It's got the township office, it's got schools, it's very good highway connections and it's been designated and has had some subdivision development in the past and promoting that and enhancing that is certainly came out through our discussions. There's also the idea of exploring the development potential of the serviced area of Rideau Avenue lands as well. One of the ideas is to promote subdivisions versus consents. Subdivisions are a more efficient way of proceeding with growth and development than one-off scattered residential severances. It's not to say that there would be no more severances, it's just that promoting an emphasis maybe on subdivisions more in key areas of the township. There's also certain areas where development has been taking place that is difficult for the township to service. Pinery Road came up multiple times as an area where it's stretching the capacity of the township to have more development in that area. We haven't explored it in detail yet and we need to do that in the future. The other thing is that there is a lot of area of the township where the severances have already been taken and that there's no room for or there's no potential for additional development in those areas. There was a desire to see maybe those areas where the number of severances has been maxed out to see if there is potential for additional development in those areas. You've had a lot of discussion to date with your planner Carl regarding secondary dwelling units. You've initiated that conversation and we're proposing to roll that into this project and come forward with policies consistent with the direction that's been expressed. Carl's reports have been spot on and they've used as an example the work that's been done in Tay Valley Township which has been not just a leader in Lanark County but a leader in Eastern Ontario in terms of advancing policies on secondary dwelling units. That is something that the township needs to look at in its official plan update. We've also been asked to look at policies regarding more sustainable development potential for green energy projects at commercial industrial scale. There's also a desire to have clear understanding of policies that talk about the constraints to development. So many times there are barriers in planning due to language that we need to break free from and make sure that people clearly understand what's expected of them and what information they need to supply when they are submitting applications for development consideration. One of the big advancements with the provincial policy statement in 2020 was the requirement to have enhanced policies regarding consultation with our First Nation communities and that would be an element that needs to be addressed in the official plan update as well. There are also policies in terms of wellhead protection and intake protection zones in both Smith Falls and Merrickville that need to be looked at to make sure you as a connecting community are ensuring that their water sources are protected as per provincial legislation. There's also a need to recognize the significance of the Rideau Canal and the policies that protect and benefit the location of the canal within your community. You're very fortunate to have that feature but it does come with a requirement to protect and enhance. There's also, we've received some updated mineral aggregate mapping from the province that needs to be looked at very carefully to make sure that you're protecting the necessary primary aggregate resources within your community and finally there is a need for natural heritage systems mapping. Right now the township has mapped wetlands and rivers and areas of natural and scientific interest but the province is now requesting that those areas be connected. There's a lot a lot of times that there's forested areas that connect wetlands and that are pathways for animals to move through and those need to be picked up in a mapping exercise and that's part of the work program that we've identified to date for you as well. That was one of the few no-ones we had going into this project was the need for natural heritage system mapping. Mr. Mayor that's the end of the list of issues. I would like to reiterate that we would like to have public comments by September 30th if that's possible though it's not a hard fast end date but it is it would help with the project management. The next steps going forward is after the end of the consultation period and when we have the majority of the agency comments in we would be putting together an issues and options report. What that would do is would highlight the issues just as we've done here but also give council some options on how to address those issues. A lot of the times there's ability to go right or left or down the middle when you're dealing with these issues and that's up to council to decide how to do that and we'll present those options to you and you can take those options, you can add to them, you can combine them, we can do lots of different things at that time but that would set the stage for what changes would actually happen to the official plan. Following that there will be a formal official plan amendment process again open to the public that would be detailing the exact changes that council is proposing to the official plan and the agencies in the public will all have an opportunity to participate in that as well. That's all I have to say at this point in time Mr. Mayor. If there are any questions or comments that come out that you would like me to address I'm here at your disposal.
